title: paratext capability
description: A capability is one plain object with no functions in it, so it can be written in a config file, generated, diffed and checked without running anybody's code. `encode` and `fallback` are templates with three rules: `{field}` is the field's value, `{field|base64}` is it base64-encoded, and `[ … ]` is emitted only when every field named inside it has a value. A capability without a `fallback` is refused at register(), because a sequence a terminal cannot read is not a feature.

name.description: How callers name it. Registering an existing name replaces it, which is how a caller corrects a detection guess we got wrong.

osc.description: The OSC code this speaks, or 'BEL' for the bell and for protocols that are not OSC at all, such as Kitty's.

when.description: When the terminal is believed to understand it. Every clause must hold; within `termProgram` and `envAny` any one match is enough. These are guesses — no terminal answers 'do you do OSC 1337' — which is why they are data a caller can replace.

tty.description: Refuse a pipe. Almost always true: a file that receives OSC gets control bytes in it.

termProgram.description: Any one of these TERM_PROGRAM values.

envAny.description: Any one of these environment variables merely being set, as VTE announces itself through VTE_VERSION.

term.description: An exact TERM, for terminals that identify that way — Kitty is xterm-kitty.

encode.description: The bytes, as a template, for a terminal that does understand.

fallback.description: What to print when it does not — PRINCIPLES rule 6. An empty string is a legitimate answer: a window title has nothing to say in a log. Absence is not, which is why this is required and may be ''.
